metadata.title: Robin half-space perturbations: a credited dimension-dependent answer to AIM Problem 1.4
metadata.description: A credited negative answer to the literal dimension-unrestricted AIM Problem 1.4. A specified nonzero smooth graph f=h/100 in R4 has spectrum [-1,infinity) at attractive Robin strength beta=1. Every connected smooth nontrivial compact half-space perturbation in ambient dimensions two and three binds below -beta^2 for every beta>0, including overhangs and compact boundary components. All compact W1,infinity graphs in dimensions at least four have absence at sufficiently weak strength depending on the graph. Exner-Minakov are credited for planar binding AND the exponential/Stokes normal-defect mechanism. Graph absence and the explicit example are also credited corollaries of Hoang-Hundertmark-Richter-Vugalter published Theorem A.6 through a complete bounded H1 geometric and Fourier bridge; Frank-Laptev flat Robin/relativistic duality, standard criticality/capacity and classical Hardy are credited. The paper includes a self-contained Hardy-trace proof and an exact earlier-theorem count certificate N<1/240. No all-strength absence for one fixed nonzero graph, general higher-dimensional nongraph classification or embedded-eigenvalue exclusion is asserted. Historical priority of exact remaining geometric formulations, novelty, worldwide open status and independent discovery remain UNKNOWN. Extensive AI assistance in solving, verification, source comparison, coding and writing. Unrefereed; no human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification.
metadata.notes: Alec Kriebel is the sole named author. OpenAI Codex AI systems were used extensively. Exact remaining geometric historical priority, novelty, worldwide open status and independent discovery are unknown. Prepared locally on 2026-10-14 before deposit or publication.
